quotes.text: First say to yourself who you wish to be, then do accordingly what you are doing.
Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions: the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running.
It is impossible for a man to begin to learn that which he thinks that he knows.
Nothing great, said Epictetus, is produced suddenly, since not even the grape or the fig is.
The good man is invincible, for he does not enter the contest where he is not stronger.
If you would be a good reader, read; if a writer, write.
Whomsoever then it is in the power of another to hinder and compel, declare that he is not free.
